'''Ronald Björn Jensen''' (April 1, 1936 – September 16, 2025) was an American mathematician who lived in Germany, primarily known for his work in [[mathematical logic]] and [[set theory]].

==Life and career==
Jensen completed a BA in economics at [[American University]] in 1959, and a Ph.D. in [[mathematics]] at the [[University of Bonn]] in 1964. His supervisor was [[Gisbert Hasenjaeger]]. Jensen taught at [[Rockefeller University]], 1969–71, and the [[University of California, Berkeley]], 1971–73. The balance of his academic career was spent in Europe at the
[[University of Bonn]], the [[University of Oslo]], the [[Albert Ludwigs University of Freiburg|University of Freiburg]], the [[University of Oxford]], and the [[Humboldt-Universität zu Berlin]], from which he retired in 2001. 

He was honored by the [[Association for Symbolic Logic]] as the first [[Gödel Lecture]]r in 1990.<ref>{{Cite journal|last=Kechris|first=Alexander S.|date=1991|title=Annual Meeting of the Association for Symbolic Logic: Berkeley, 1990|url=https://www.jstor.org/stable/2274945|journal=[[The Journal of Symbolic Logic]]|volume=56|issue=1|pages=361–371|doi=10.2307/2274945|jstor=2274945 |s2cid=98210 |issn=0022-4812|quote=Moreover, the Gödel Lecture, a new feature of the ASL Annual Meetings, was inaugurated this year. The first Gödel lecture was given by Ronald Jensen, who spoke on ''Inner Models and Large Cardinals.''|url-access=subscription}}</ref> In 2015, the European Set Theory Society awarded him and [[John R. Steel]] the [[Hausdorff Medal]] for their paper ''K without the measurable''.<ref>
{{cite journal|author=Ronald Jensen and John Steel|title='''K''' without the measurable|journal=[[The Journal of Symbolic Logic]]|volume=78|issue=3|pages=708-734|url=https://www.jstor.org/stable/43303677|year=2013}}</ref>

Jensen died on September 16, 2025, at the age of 89.<ref>{{cite web |title=Ronald B. Jensen |url=https://www.math.uni-bonn.de/~raesch/jensen/ |website=Mathematical Institute of the University of Bonn |access-date=27 September 2025}}</ref>

==Results==
Jensen's better-known results include the:
* [[Axiomatic set theory]] [[New Foundations|NFU]], a variant of [[New Foundations]] (NF) where [[Axiom of extensionality|extensionality]] is weakened to allow several sets with no elements, and the proof of NFU's [[consistency]] relative to [[Peano arithmetic]];
* Fine structure theory of the [[constructible universe]] '''L'''. This work led to his being awarded in 2003 the [[Leroy P Steele Prize|Leroy P. Steele Prize for Seminal Contribution to Research]] of the [[American Mathematical Society]] for his 1972 paper titled "The fine structure of the constructible hierarchy";
*Definitions and proofs of various [[Infinitary combinatorics|infinitary combinatorial principle]]s in '''L''', including [[diamondsuit|diamond]] <math>\diamondsuit</math>, [[global square|square]], and [[morass (set theory)|morass]];
* [[Jensen's covering theorem]] for '''L''';
* General theory of [[core model]]s and the construction of the [[Dodd–Jensen core model]];
* Consistency of the [[continuum hypothesis]] plus [[Suslin's hypothesis]];
* Technique of [[coding the universe by a real]].

==Selected publications==
===Articles===
* Ronald Jensen, 1969, « On the Consistency of a Slight(?) Modification of Quine's NF », ''Synthese 19'': 250–263. With discussion by Quine. {{doi|10.1007/BF00568059}}	
* The fine structure of the constructible hierarchy, Annals of Mathematical Logic, vol 4, Issue 3, August 1972, pp.&nbsp;229–308 {{doi|10.1016/0003-4843(72)90001-0}}
* with Anthony J. Dodd: The core model, Annals of Mathematical Logic, vol 20, 1981, pp.&nbsp;43–75. {{doi|10.1016/0003-4843(81)90011-5}}
* with Anthony J. Dodd: The covering lemma for K, Annals of Mathematical Logic, vol 22, 1982, pp.&nbsp;1–30. {{doi|10.1016/0003-4843(82)90013-4}}
* Inner models and large cardinals. [[Bulletin of Symbolic Logic]] vol 1, Issue 4 (1995): 393-407. {{doi|10.2307/421129}}
* with John R. Steel: ''K without the measurable'', The Journal of Symbolic Logic, vol 78, Issue 3, 2013, pp.&nbsp;708–734. {{doi|10.2178/jsl.7803020}}

===Books===
* ''Modelle der Mengenlehre. Widerspruchsfreiheit und Unabhängigkeit der Kontinuumshypothese und des Auswahlaxioms.'' (Lecture Notes in Mathematics; vol. 37). Springer, Berlin 1967.
*as editor with Alexander Pestel: Set theory and model theory: proceedings of an informal symposium held at Bonn, June 1–3, 1979. Berlin; New York: Springer-Verlag, 1981.
* with Aaron Beller and Philip Welch: [https://books.google.com/books?id=IBHkbaibP4EC ''Coding the Universe.''] Cambridge University Press, Cambridge 1982, {{ISBN|0-521-28040-0}}.<ref>{{cite journal|title=Review: ''Coding the universe'' by A.
